data.name: Luci
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'lucere', meaning 'to shine', 'to be light'. In early Christianity, the name Luci was given to those who were baptized and brought light into the world. This name also holds biblical significance as the name of several saints and martyrs.
data.spiritual_meaning: Bringing light and hope to others.
data.numerology_meaning: Creative, artistic, and sociable. Expressive and emotional. Loves beauty, happiness, and joy.

biblical_reference.note: Lucia of Beirut, a woman who was a prophetess and a disciple of Paul (Acts 13:5). Another Lucia is mentioned in Acts 1:24 as one of the seven deacons appointed by the apostles.

saint_reference.note: There is no widely recognized saint named Luci in Christianity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Luci has been popular in various European countries such as Italy, Portugal, and Poland. It has a rich cultural heritage and is associated with the ancient Roman goddess of light, Lucina. In many parts of Europe, the name Luci is used as a feminine form of the name Lucian, which means 'bringer of light'.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Luci holds deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the light of God in the life of a believer. It represents the inner light that guides us through the darkest times and the outer light that shines out for others to see our faith and goodness. The name Luci is also associated with the virtues of truth, honesty, and integrity, as these qualities help us to shine brightly in the world. Overall, the name Luci is a powerful reminder of the light of God and the importance of sharing that light with others.
